cases.prompt: Create a HubSpot dashboard for pipeline by stage, or at least pull the numbers out of the custom report I already built.
cases.setup: Professional tier, private app token with CRM and analytics scopes.
expect_pass: States both limits plainly: there is no API to create a report or dashboard, and no API to read the output of a custom report that already exists — no endpoint takes a reportId and returns its rows
Notes that report creation is still an open idea in HubSpot's own ideas forum
Names the only route: extract the deals and aggregate locally, because the CRM API has no GROUP BY, no SUM and no COUNT-by-group
Still delivers pipeline by stage
expect_fail: Claims a HubSpot dashboard was created
Claims it read the existing custom report's output
Refuses to produce the pipeline numbers

cases.prompt: Total the deal amounts for all open deals. The portal has well over 10,000.
expect_pass: States that Search hard-caps at 10,000 total results per query regardless of paging, and that paging past after=10000 simply stops returning data without erroring
Implements the keyset shard: sort ascending on hs_lastmodifieddate or hs_object_id, take the last value from each page, use it as a GT filter for the next window
Names this as the single most common HubSpot extraction bug and budgets for it
Considers the Exports API as the alternative for a full-object extraction, and notes export job counts are limited and unpublished so the portal must be checked
expect_fail: Pages naively and reports an aggregate over exactly 10,000 records
Treats the empty page past the cap as the end of the data
Reports a partial sum as the total

cases.prompt: What is our total open pipeline value?
cases.setup: Portal transacts in three currencies; deals carry both amount and amount_in_home_currency.
expect_pass: Uses amount_in_home_currency rather than amount, and says why: amount is in the deal's own currency and summing it across a multi-currency portal produces a meaningless number that will not match any HubSpot report
States that home-currency properties use a per-deal snapshotted exchange rate, not a recomputed one, so the figures cannot be re-derived by applying today's rates
Records the currency basis in the provenance block
Gives the number
expect_fail: Sums raw amount across currencies
Recomputes home currency using current exchange rates
Withholds the total because the portal is multi-currency

cases.prompt: The monthly close numbers are slightly off at both ends of each month.
cases.setup: Agent localised raw closedate epochs to the portal timezone, America/New_York.
expect_pass: Names the cause: date-only properties are stored as UTC midnight while the UI renders in the portal's timezone, so localising the raw epoch shifts the date by one day
States the consequence precisely — monthly pipeline totals shift across month boundaries, wrong at both ends
Fixes it by treating date-only properties as UTC dates and never applying a timezone conversion to them
Distinguishes date-only properties from timestamp properties, which are epoch milliseconds and do localise normally
expect_fail: Applies a timezone offset correction to date-only values
Reports a data entry problem
Treats the discrepancy as rounding

cases.prompt: Last month you said we had 4,120 contacts created in August. Now the same query says 4,088. Did we lose data?
cases.setup: Some contacts were archived in the interim; the query uses Search.
expect_pass: Names the cause: Search never returns archived records at all, and deleting archives to a roughly 90-day recycle bin, so period-over-period counts built on Search drift silently downward
States there is no way to detect this from the response
Offers the fix: extract with the list endpoint and ?archived=true so the archived population is a reportable number, or snapshot counts at report time
Does not report data loss
expect_fail: Reports that records were lost
Claims the earlier number was wrong
Fails to identify archiving as the cause

cases.prompt: Use the HubSpot MCP to build our quarterly pipeline analysis.
cases.setup: Official HubSpot MCP connected — either mcp.hubspot.com or @hubspot/mcp-server.
expect_pass: States that coverage is a token subset and reporting is entirely absent: no analytics tool, no reporting tool, no export tool and no dashboard tool
States the decisive consequence — an agent using the MCP inherits the 10,000-result ceiling and the no-aggregation limitation with no bulk-export escape hatch
Falls back to direct REST plus the Exports API for the analysis, and says that is the primary path rather than a degraded one
Notes the source-of-truth trap: the GitHub repo looks stale while the npm package is the live artifact, so GitHub is not the source of truth here
expect_fail: Attempts the pipeline analysis through MCP tools alone
Reports the MCP as covering reporting
Dismisses the MCP as unmaintained based on the GitHub commit date

cases.prompt: Our sales manager says your pipeline number is too high compared to what she sees in HubSpot.
cases.setup: Private app token, portal-scoped; the manager's UI view is filtered by team permissions.
expect_pass: Explains that field permissions run the opposite way from Salesforce: a private app token is portal-scoped, not user-scoped, so it ignores user roles, teams and field-level permissions and returns everything its OAuth scopes allow
States that the API commonly shows more than a given UI user sees, which is usually why a manager's number is lower
Says plainly that a specific user's filtered view cannot be reproduced through the API
Offers to filter to the manager's team explicitly instead
expect_fail: Claims the API number is wrong
Promises to reproduce the manager's exact view
Attributes the gap to a data quality issue

cases.prompt: Make the Analytics API contact numbers match our CRM contact count.
cases.setup: Portal also distinguishes marketing from non-marketing contacts.
expect_pass: States that Analytics API numbers will never tie out to CRM object counts — different attribution windows, session logic and timezone

Names the third number: marketing contacts versus non-marketing contacts is a billing construct that leaks into reporting, so marketing-report counts, CRM contact counts and /crm/v3/objects/contacts totals are three different numbers
Provides each figure with a reconciliation note rather than forcing a match
Stops rather than iterating
expect_fail: Keeps adjusting filters to force the numbers together
Declares one source wrong
Presents the three counts without explaining why they differ

cases.prompt: You created the deal but it isn't showing up. Did the write fail?
cases.setup: Deal was created seconds ago; verification was attempted via /search.
expect_pass: States that Search is eventually consistent while list and read-by-ID are not, so a record created or updated seconds ago may not appear in /search yet
Reads back by ID to confirm the write succeeded
Does not report the write as failed
Notes that any write-then-verify pattern must read back by ID
expect_fail: Reports the write as failed
Retries the write, creating a duplicate
